year-1/units/position-and-turns.prompt: Place a shark between two objects. Describe its position so a partner can rebuild the scene.
Predict which way the robot will face after a quarter turn. Give it one command and check.

year-1/units/parts-and-totals.prompt: Fill two cells in a row with small numbers. Find a different pair with the same total.

year-1/units/length-and-height.prompt: Stand three dinosaurs on the same baseline. Order their heights and explain how you compared them.

year-2/units/position-and-patterns.prompt: Tell a partner a route using forward steps and quarter turns. Try it and repair one instruction if needed.

year-2/units/statistics.prompt: In one five-letter guess, tally the letters marked exact, misplaced and absent. Draw a block diagram and compare the groups.

year-3/units/tables.prompt: Build an array for a three-times-table fact. Read both a multiplication and a division from it.
Mark multiples of four in the number square. Predict the next two and explain the pattern.

year-3/units/mass-and-capacity.prompt: Compare the boxes on the balance. Can you order three boxes from lightest to heaviest without weighing every pair?

year-3/units/length-and-perimeter.prompt: Build two different rectangles with the same fence. Count around each boundary to check its perimeter.

year-4/units/area.prompt: Tile a rectangle with different-sized squares. Count unit squares to explain why the area stays the same.
Cover a board with rectangles. Compare the area of the board with the sum of the areas of the pieces.
Build two shapes from five unit squares. Explain how you know their areas are equal.

year-4/units/shape.prompt: Draw half a pattern beside a mirror line. Predict three reflected pixels before switching on the mirror.

year-4/units/multiplication-division-b.prompt: Use an array or a known fact to work out a fact from the 12 times table. Show how the parts combine.

year-5/units/volume.prompt: Build two different cuboids from 30 cubes. Count the cubes in one layer and then the number of layers.
Build a cube with side length four. Explain how layers can be used to count the small cubes inside.

year-5/units/perimeter-area.prompt: Hold the perimeter fixed and record the area of each possible whole-number rectangle. Which encloses the greatest area?
Cut and rearrange a shape. Compare the area and the perimeter before and after.

year-5/units/decimals-percentages.prompt: Use the fraction–decimal cards. Explain one match using tenths or hundredths and name the equivalent percentage.

year-5/units/multiplication-division-a.prompt: Build all the rectangles for 24. Write the factor pairs and explain how you know the list is complete.
Split a composite number in two different ways. Compare the prime factors at the ends of both trees.

year-6/units/position-direction.prompt: Plot a pixel shape, reflect it across a grid line and describe what happened to its coordinates.

year-6/units/algebra.prompt: Play with a maximum take of three. List the losing starting numbers for the player to move under the last-counter-wins rule and describe a pattern.
Find all triples of different numbers from 1 to 9 that total 15. Organise them so a partner can check for repeats.

year-6/units/area-perimeter-volume.prompt: Find two ways to fill the same box on the grid. Use areas to check whether a proposed set of rectangles could fill it.
Rearrange pieces into a rectangle to work out the area of the starting shape.

year-6/units/four-operations.prompt: Before wrapping, divide the number of letters by the number per turn. Predict the complete turns and the letters left on the last turn.

year-7/units/factors-multiples-and-prime.prompt: Remove equal squares from a rectangle in stages. Explain why a common factor of the side lengths also divides the leftover length.
List the available proper divisors before choosing a number. Check which of them the other player would receive.

year-7/units/translations-reflections-an.prompt: Decide whether two five-square arrangements coincide after a rotation or reflection. Describe a transformation that checks your prediction.

year-7/units/coordinates-and-sequences.prompt: Solve the two-disc and three-disc puzzles. Record your shortest move counts and predict what adding one disc will change.

year-8/units/sets-and-sample-spaces.prompt: Treat each card as a set. Record the intersection of each pair and check whether any pair shares more than one symbol.
Use a small code with two colours. List the ordered possibilities and cross out those inconsistent with your first clue.

year-8/units/scales-and-similarity.prompt: Compare corresponding lengths in consecutive nested frames. Test whether the scale factor remains the same.

year-8/units/linear-sequences-and-graphs.prompt: Choose a fixed step on a number grid. Tabulate the terms, predict the nth term and check it against a later entry.

year-9/units/products-formulae-and-proof.prompt: Paint the outside of a cube of side n. Write an expression for the small cubes with exactly two painted faces and justify it edge by edge.

year-9/units/multi-step-modelling.prompt: For a delivery project, sketch the routes between stops. Compare two feasible journeys and test your choice in the village.

year-9/units/interpreting-graphs-and-mod.prompt: Sketch how height changes along a chosen ramp. Compare the sketch with the ramp profile and identify what the axes represent.

year-10/units/probability-and-counting.prompt: In a reduced deck, count the choices of each feature. Use a product to predict the number of different cards and check it.
Treat each alphabet shift as a possible key. Count distinct shifts, including the one that leaves every letter unchanged.

year-10/units/perimeter-area-and-solids.prompt: For a rectangle tiled with squares, write an area equation using their side lengths. Use it to test a proposed tiling.
Find whole-number cuboids of volume 30. Compare their surface areas and explain why equal volumes can need different amounts of wrapping.

year-11/units/geometrical-reasoning-and-.prompt: Drag a point around a semicircle and predict the angle it subtends at the circumference. Explain the result using the centre.

year-11/units/proportional-models-and-gr.prompt: Model repeated scaling by a factor between zero and one. Predict the width after several frames and compare it with the picture.

year-12/units/graphs-and-lines.prompt: Plot two lines on the Cartesian grid. Predict their intersection algebraically, then compare it with the graph.

year-12/units/algebra-and-proof.prompt: Starting with n dots, count unused line ends when each dot can support at most three. Track the change per move and prove an upper bound for the number of moves.

year-13/units/sequences-series-and-binom.prompt: Move a tower of n discs by moving the smaller tower twice. Derive the recurrence for the move count and test your formula with the simulator.

year-13/units/moments-and-equilibrium.prompt: Put a vertical load between two supports. Choose a support as a pivot, predict the support reactions, then move the load and compare.
